name: sedation_level
intended_use: Research and decision SUPPORT: how much does a resting EEG resemble awake vs propofol-sedated EEG of healthy volunteers (two laboratories).
not_for: detecting consciousness or covert awareness in patients
any clinical decision on its own

training_data.population: healthy adults under propofol, two laboratories

labels: sedated = moderate sedation (Cambridge) or rest under propofol before an awakening (Oslo); awake = baseline/recovery/eyes-closed awake; Cambridge mild not used
known_limits: 40 healthy people in two laboratories; wide intervals
never validated on patients; EEG slowing in dementia can look sedated-like
unfamiliar-EEG flag catches noise, dead channels and many bad electrodes but NOT shuffled electrode order (region averages hide it); check the montage

unfamiliar_eeg_detector.method: PCA, Hotelling T-squared and SPE; epoch flagged above the training percentile; recording called unfamiliar if more than 25 % of its epochs are flagged; non-finite features always flagged
